answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation bond tied to a verifiable work history — an atlas of past attestations — rather than free account creation. Newcomers start with near-zero weight and must earn trust through slow, orchard-like cultivation of real interactions, so cloning identities yields no immediate power. A relic identity with no recent attestation decays, so attackers cannot stockpile cheap old accounts and must pay the same slow cost for every fake.
